speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for Transport in respect of the addition of another two ride-hailing operators in 2025 (a) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the impact on the availability of private hire cars on the road and ride fares; and (b) what is the Ministry's assessment of the impact on the availability of Certificates of Entitlement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The first is, how does the Ministry balance the earnings of drivers or potential entrants and pre-existing ones, and the availability of public transport to the public?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In determining the entry of new private hire operators, or ride-hail operators, is there an optimal number?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The second supplementary question, did the previous entrance of other operators over the last years cause any salient increase in COE prices?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Fares too reflect the balance of supply and demand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Why do I say that we do not have plans to cap the number of platform operators?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we require that drivers are allowed to multi-home, that they are not tied to a particular operator.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have mentioned earlier, in the reply, the entry of two new ride-hail service operators actually means that there will be more choices for drivers and commuters, and it will benefit them.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also ensure that the operators are transparent about the fares and commissions, so that the drivers can make informed decisions about when to drive and what trips from which platform to accept, so that they can maximise their earnings based on the platforms they choose, as well as, of course, their driving habits or driving preferences.
